newsitem.title: FRANCE: France ready to help evacuate foreigners in Kabul.
newsitem.headline: France ready to help evacuate foreigners in Kabul.

text.p: France said on Wednesday it was prepared to help evacuate foreigners from Kabul as the Afghan Taleban militia battled to the eastern edge of the capital.
"It seems that the Taleban have entered the suburbs of Kabul," a ministry statement said.

"The international community, which is made up almost exclusively of non-governmental organisations (about 130 people of whom 30 are French), has begun to evacuate the capital as a safety measure," it said.
The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) was sending planes to Kabul to evacuate foreigners.

"France, which has a charge d'affaires on the spot, is prepared to put the necessary means in place to take part in this evacuation and thus contribute to the safety of foreign citizens in Kabul," it said. It gave no details.

The Taleban attack is threatening the survival of President Burhanuddin Rabbani's government. Rebel sources said government jets were bombing the Taleban, who were attacking Kabul from the east, south and southwest.
